requirements.rationale: Evidence lists key hyperparameters (β_t schedule, T, dropout, data augmentation, optimizer, learning rate) and notes that most were tuned on CIFAR‑10 then transferred to other datasets, directly addressing which hyperparameters matter and their cross‑dataset adaptability.

decisions.decision: Is DDPM sampling a good replacement for current GAN generation stack?
decisions.answer: Conditionally. Quality is GAN-level, but sampling needs ~1000 network evaluations per image, so for latency/throughput–critical stacks it is not a good drop‑in replacement; for offline or non‑real‑time use it can be a strong alternative.
decisions.notes: Quality: Diffusion model with trainable L reaches IS 9.46 and FID 3.17 on CIFAR‑10, close to StyleGAN2‑ADA (IS 9.74, FID 3.26). Authors state their FID 3.17 gives better sample quality than most models, including many class‑conditional ones, indicating GAN‑competitive quality. Sampling: Experiments fix T=1000, and sampling requires 1000 neural net evaluations, far more than a single GAN forward pass. Rate–distortion table shows quality degrades sharply when steps are reduced (RMSE ~0.95 at 1000 steps vs ~38 at 500), so naive step reduction to speed up sampling significantly hurts quality. Training: Objective is a variational bound on NLL, not adversarial, so it avoids GAN‑style instability; a reweighted objective improves sample quality. Hyperparameters: β schedule and T are fixed globally; most hyperparameter search was done on CIFAR‑10 then transferred to other datasets, suggesting some robustness but also that tuning may be needed per domain. Overall, diffusion is not a straightforward replacement where low latency or high throughput is critical, but is attractive where offline, high‑quality generation is acceptable.
